title: IP Law Firm MBHB Launches Dedicated Quantum, Optics, and Semiconductors Practice Group in Chicago - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IP law firm MBHB has launched a Chicago-based Quantum, Optics, and Semiconductors Practice Group to serve the regional hub around the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park, where PsiQuantum is anchor tenant. The article says quantum patenting is getting harder as research turns into products, especially around 35 U.S.C. § 101 eligibility and federal funding strings.

themes.theme: Legal services follow the Chicago quantum hub

insights.claim: MBHB set up a dedicated Quantum, Optics, and Semiconductors Practice Group in Chicago, co-chaired by Andrew Velzen and Aaron Gin. It will serve the hub anchored by the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park, where PsiQuantum is anchor tenant and partners such as IBM are deploying commercial quantum infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Specialized professional services forming around IQMP suggest the Chicago quantum cluster is maturing.
insights.locator: Intellectual property law firm McDonnell Boehnen

insights.claim: As quantum innovation moves from basic research to proprietary products, firms must handle 35 U.S.C. § 101 eligibility by grounding patent claims in physical apparatus, such as cryogenic controls and photonic packaging, rather than abstract algorithms.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hardware-anchored claims may give quantum companies stronger IP moats than algorithm patents.
insights.quote: firms must navigate 35 U.S.C. § 101 eligibility by grounding claims in physical apparatuses—such as cryogenic controls and photonic packaging—rather than abstract algorithms
insights.locator: The practice addresses growing patenting challenges

insights.claim: Publicly funded quantum work brings federal march-in rights, Bayh-Dole compliance and export controls, which complicate commercialization and licensing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Spin-outs built on government-funded research carry IP encumbrances that investors should check.
insights.locator: The practice addresses growing patenting challenges
